title: Why does Unity MCP suck so bad?
author: thefirstrevanite
selftext:
It is literally unusable and bloats context like nothing else. Every open source alternative I tried so far and even my own CLI solutions feel so much more mature, am I the only one that thinks that?

How can they screw this up so bad?

replies.author: thefirstrevanite
replies.body: Didnt test it but seems like a very big thing, I stick to UCP (my own tooling) though for lightweight controls

comments.author: VinWareApps
comments.body: I don’t know but you’re right, it does. And the fact they make you pay for it is ridiculous

comments.author: Mindestiny
comments.body:
It's still in beta, and honestly... it's a tough value proposition.  Unity .assets are \*notoriously\* hard to parse as raw data and there's so much noisy caching going on in the background that trying often gives you stale values and incorrect scene state. 

They're really gonna have to do a lot of work on it to make it a quality product and better than just pointing Claude at your project folder (which is already a crapshoot).

replies.author: thefirstrevanite
replies.body: Yeah, if I didn't have to pay for that slop...

comments.author: Cubey42
comments.body: Oh I dunno about bloating context but overall it's been fine for my use.

replies.author: thefirstrevanite
replies.body: What do you usually do with it?

replies.author: Cubey42
replies.body: Well so far I've: choreographed a cutscene for a transition between phases of the game. Crafted a map generator that caters to my game style. Added multiple functional layers of systems of quite a variety not limited but including UI, shaders, computational, ECS. Mesh generation for general blockout and first pass using references. In my experience they're pretty much hasn't been a nail I couldn't hammer. Sometimes things might not go perfectly or maybe the AI is being particularly lazy but I haven't really ran into an obstacle I couldn't overcome though again like I said I wasn't really concerned as much about context tokens but I've been working with it for about 8 months now and I'm pretty excited to show what I've been doing in the near future

comments.author: Reinfeldx
comments.body: The big picture issue is that Unity is a lost, rudderless company at the management level.

comments.author: BertJohn
comments.body:
What are you trying to do with it thats failing so bad? 

  
Ive used it to create prefabs with custom tooling implementation and set up entire animators/custom animators through animancer/cas and it succeeds 100%. Even gauging sizes, which no other MCP bridge has successfully implemented. Unity's built in beats all the open source and paid versions ive used so far.

comments.author: CCB0x45
comments.body: Ive had pretty good luck with unity mcp? I use it a ton, the only thing I dont like is it only allows 1 connection at a time, and that I have to pay for it which is silly.

comments.author: blanktarget
comments.body: I use a free mcp for unity and it's awesome. Not paying for this nonsense.

replies.author: blanktarget
replies.body:
No it's not. You maybe see on a trial or paying and not knowing it. 
Here's some info:
Unity's official Model Context Protocol (MCP) server is paywalled behind a Unity AI subscription. To use the built-in MCP server feature within the Unity AI Assistant package, users must have a paid tier despite utilizing their own local compute and external LLMs.The Official Paywall StructureUnity Personal: Requires a separate $10/month Unity AI subscription. It restricts usage to 1 concurrent MCP connection.

replies.author: slipperyslips
replies.body: My mistake i misread unity for unreal

comments.author: LouisGameDevX
comments.body:
I think a lot depends on how you use it. I’ve had much better results when I treat MCP as a bridge into Unity instead of expecting Claude to constantly inspect and understand the entire project.

I keep each task focused, tell Claude what it actually needs to inspect, and start a new chat when the context gets messy. I also don’t have it repeatedly read the whole project when I’m only changing one system.

MCP has saved me a lot of time creating objects, setting things up, testing and making changes inside Unity, but it still needs direction. What specifically is causing the context bloat for you?
